nodes.title: Unlock Microsoft for Startups Milestone 3 ($25k + 2-year extension) by holding 7 candidate services (5 required + 2 spare), each ≥ $1 EVERY UTC day for 60 days, counted as Cost Management ServiceNames. The 7 services: Container Apps (taxila-web, guard only), PostgreSQL (taxila-cin-pg, optional downsize to B2s), Container Registry (taxilacr → Premium), Foundry Models, Foundry Tools and Storage (a capped daily ACA job, m3-keeper, spends $1.35 / $1.35 / $1.25 under a $2 cap, from what the APIs report), and Virtual Machines (optional D2as_v5, owner-gated). An ACA job m3-verify reads Cost Management daily and alerts the Owner role. All of it runs inside Azure with no Claude session. scripts/m3.mjs is dry-run by default. Reverse if Microsoft changes or clarifies the rule (e.g. counts by resource or meter, not ServiceName), if Cost Management shows Foundry Models and Foundry Tools collapsing into one service, if the 180-day deadline has already passed (open-r7-m3-verification-deadline), or if the credit cannot cover the 60 days.

Microsoft for Startups milestone rules, read 2026-11-05 from https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/startups/standard-benefits/unlock-more-benefits (page dated 2026-11-03). M3 $25k: ≥ 5 workloads, each ≥ $1, every day for 60 continuous days; dropping one below $1 drops the count. The page does not say how a 'unique service' is counted. M2 clause: not qualifying for M3 within 180 days of business verification cancels the sponsorship and converts the subscription to pay-as-you-go. M4 $50k: the same rule with 7 workloads; milestones can be skipped. M3 adds a one-time 2-year extension.

The M3 deadline is unknown. If business verification was 2026-07-08 (the sponsorship's start), the 180 days end 2027-01-04 and the 60-day clock must start by 2026-11-06. On 2026-10-24 only 2 services held ≥ $1/day. We do not know the real verification date, or whether a clause published around 2026-11-03 applies to a July sponsorship. The owner must check the Founders Hub milestone tracker.

Container Registry retail, eastus2: Premium Registry Unit $1.6666/day (meter 2f8e1105), Standard $0.6666/day (984c39d8), Basic $0.1666/day (5c9e7a65). Premium is the only tier that holds $1/day; it adds $1.50/day over today's Basic. n = 2 reads (discovery filter + meterId re-check), Azure Retail Prices API, 2026-11-05.

PostgreSQL Flexible retail, centralindia: D2ds_v5 2 vCore $0.251/h (fdd9e8a2); Burstable B1ms $0.0245/h (27c18f86), B2s $0.098/h (3e7d2ab5), B2ms $0.196/h, B4ms $0.392/h; storage $0.131/GB-month (94cadb5b). With 64 GB: today $6.30/day, B2s $2.63/day, B1ms $0.86/day (under the $1.25 bar, refused). n = 2 reads, Retail Prices API, 2026-11-05.

Linux VM retail, centralindia: Standard_D2as_v5 $0.0556/h = $1.334/day (70be92d6), the cheapest common x64 size ≥ $1.25/day. Near misses: D2als_v6 $0.052/h = $1.248/day, B2s $0.0448/h = $1.075/day. E4 Standard SSD disk $2.64/month = $0.087/day, billed under Storage. n = 7,555 VM rows read (all pages), then a meterId re-check; Retail Prices API, 2026-11-05.

Storage retail, eastus2, General Block Blob v2 Hot LRS: 'LRS List and Create Container Operations' $0.05 per 10,000 (meter 3d7aa86c, the same meter as Hot LRS Write Operations). Microsoft's REST-to-price map puts ListBlobs in the 'List and create container' class. $1.25/day = 250,000 List Blobs calls. n = 2 reads, Retail Prices API + learn.microsoft.com map-rest-apis-transaction-categories (ms.date 2025-05-14), 2026-11-05.

Speech TTS retail: ServiceName 'Foundry Tools', product 'Azure Speech', 'S1 Neural Text To Speech Characters' $15 per 1M characters in both centralindia and eastus2 (meter 0f98e708). Neural HD is $22 (ad55d150). $1.35/day = 90,000 characters, about 128 requests of the keeper's fixed paragraphs. n = 2 reads, Retail Prices API, 2026-11-05.

Foundry Models retail, eastus2, GlobalStandard short context. gpt-5.6-luna (taxila-fast = DEPLOY_FAST): input $0.20, cached $0.02, output $1.20 per 1M tokens (1e606a78 / 97d64f6e / 0edf673f). gpt-5.6-sol (taxila-brain = DEPLOY_BRAIN): $4 / $0.40 / $20. These match server/cost/prices.js. $1.35/day on luna ≈ 1.1M output tokens (~280 calls); on sol ≈ 67,500 (~17 calls). n = 2 reads, Retail Prices API, 2026-11-05.

tests/m3-plan.test.mjs, 15/15 pass. Both in-job scripts were run end to end against a fake Azure (a blob store with ETags, chat, TTS, List Blobs, Cost Management with nextLink). Results: the am run reached each target under the $2 cap, and its ledger matched the spend the fake reported to 1e-3; the pm run made 0 extra calls; an unreadable ledger led to exactly one blind spend per day across reruns, and the pm run skipped; a failing primary deployment fell back to taxila-brain; a lost ledger write never let the retry pass the cap. The verifier printed M3-OK with streak 13 and a written report, and alerted on a dip, a missing ledger, a reset and a failed query. The in-job copies of plan.js functions match it (toString and fixtures). NOT measured live: no Azure credentials in the session; nothing was applied.

md.decisions:
## dc-r7-m3-credit-unlock (2026-11-05, round 7 M3)

Milestone 3 ($25,000 plus a 2-year extension) needs at least 5 Azure workloads, each at or above $1 every day for 60 continuous days (fd-r7-m3-rule-2026-11-05). On 2026-10-24 only Container Apps and PostgreSQL held that (ms-azure-spend-2026-10-24). We count a workload as one Cost Management ServiceName. Microsoft does not say how it counts, so this is a proxy. It is also why we carry 2 spares.

The portfolio has 7 services:
- **Container Apps.** taxila-web is always on. `apply` only checks minReplicas >= 1.
- **PostgreSQL.** taxila-cin-pg, $6.30/day. An owner-gated `--pg-downsize` refuses any SKU under $1.25/day; B2s is $2.63.
- **Container Registry.** taxilacr moves to Premium, $1.67/day. Standard is $0.67, too low.
- **Foundry Models, Foundry Tools and Storage.** One ACA job, m3-keeper, runs at 03:17 and 15:17 UTC. It spends chat tokens on DEPLOY_FAST, Speech neural TTS characters, and List Blobs operations, to $1.35 / $1.35 / $1.25 under a $2 cap per lane.
- **Virtual Machines.** Owner-gated: D2as_v5 at $1.33/day in a new RG, no public IP, no inbound rule.

Rules for the keeper:
- Spend is computed from what each API reports.
- A per-day ledger blob carries write-ahead pending amounts, so a crash or a lost write can only under-spend.
- An unreadable ledger means one blind spend in the am run and a skip in the pm run.

m3-verify runs daily inside Azure and needs no Claude session:
- It reads 66 days of Cost Management by ServiceName.
- It computes the strict clock: one fixed set of >= 5 services, each >= $1, on every closed day.
- It alerts the Owner role when fewer than 6 services held $1, a portfolio service was under $1.10, the keeper ledger was short, or the clock reset.

Cost: +$5.51/day (6 services) to +$6.93/day (7). The downsize saves $3.67/day.

Why this design:
- Fixed resources are cheapest per service but give no per-day control.
- A keeper job gives exact daily spend on the token- and operation-billed services.
- The VM and the second AI service are the hedge against Microsoft counting differently.

Reverse if:
- Microsoft changes or clarifies the rule (counts by resource, meter or category);
- Cost Management shows Foundry Models and Foundry Tools as one service;
- the 180-day deadline has passed (open-r7-m3-verification-deadline);
- or the remaining credit cannot cover the 60 days without converting the subscription to pay-as-you-go.

Constrained by dc-owner-2026-10-27-azure-soft: the owner says yes to `--vm` and `--pg-downsize`; nothing is deleted.
md.measurements:
## fd-r7-m3-rule-2026-11-05 (finding, read 2026-11-05)

Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/startups/standard-benefits/unlock-more-benefits (ms.date 2026-11-03).
- Milestone 3 ($25k): "Use at least 5 Azure workloads over a sustained period of 60 days." The clock starts once each workload has at least $1 in spend, and "every workload must stay above $1 in spend for all 60 days". "If any workload drops below the threshold, you fall under the required number."
- A workload is "an Azure service you actively use in your solution. Each unique service counts." How a service is identified is not stated.
- The Milestone 2 clause: "If you don't qualify for Milestone 3 ... within 180 days of Business Verification, the sponsorship is cancelled and the subscription is converted to pay-as-you-go."
- Milestone 4 ($50k) is the same rule with 7 workloads, and milestones can be skipped. Milestone 3 brings a one-time 2-year extension.

## ms-r7-m3-price-acr-2026-11-05 (2026-11-05, Retail Prices API, n = 2 reads)

Filter: `serviceName eq 'Container Registry' and armRegionName eq 'eastus2'`, re-checked by meterId with `node scripts/m3.mjs prices`.
- Premium Registry Unit: $1.6666/day (2f8e1105-47d0-4105-a934-b2175c766a71).
- Standard: $0.6666/day.
- Basic: $0.1666/day.

Only Premium holds $1/day.

## ms-r7-m3-price-pg-2026-11-05 (2026-11-05, Retail Prices API, n = 2 reads)

Filters: `serviceName eq 'Azure Database for PostgreSQL' and armRegionName eq 'centralindia'` with `contains(productName,'Flexible Server Burstable BS Series')`, `contains(meterName,'Storage')`, and `contains(productName,'Ddsv5') and skuName eq '2 vCore'`.
- D2ds_v5: $0.251/h.
- Burstable: B1ms $0.0245/h, B2s $0.098/h, B2ms $0.196/h, B4ms $0.392/h.
- Storage: $0.131/GB-month.

Per day with 64 GB (730 h/month): today $6.30; B2s $2.63; B1ms $0.86, under $1.25, so `--pg-downsize` refuses it. New 2026-10 Burstable v2 rows (Basv2 / Balsv2 / Batsv2 / Bafsv2, priced per vCore) were seen but not used: their SKU names were not verified.

## ms-r7-m3-price-vm-2026-11-05 (2026-11-05, Retail Prices API, n = 7,555 rows + 1 re-check)

Filter: `serviceName eq 'Virtual Machines' and armRegionName eq 'centralindia' and priceType eq 'Consumption'`, all pages, Linux rows only.
- Standard_D2as_v5: $0.0556/h = $1.334/day (70be92d6-4fad-569d-8eb6-87cf609ea508). The cheapest common x64 size at or above $1.25/day.
- Near misses: D2als_v6 $1.248/day; B2s $1.075/day; F1ads_v7 $1.33/day (NVMe-only family).
- E4 Standard SSD disk: $2.64/month (5909273e), about $0.087/day, billed under Storage.

## ms-r7-m3-price-storage-ops-2026-11-05 (2026-11-05, Retail Prices API, n = 2 reads)

Filter: `serviceName eq 'Storage' and armRegionName eq 'eastus2' and productName eq 'General Block Blob v2' and skuName eq 'Hot LRS'`.
- 'LRS List and Create Container Operations': $0.05 per 10K (3d7aa86c-0e9d-4139-b59f-cc5bad92b873). This is the same meter id as Hot LRS Write Operations.
- Microsoft's REST-to-price map (map-rest-apis-transaction-categories) puts ListBlobs in 'List and create container'.
- $1.25 = 250,000 calls. taxilaforge is StorageV2 Standard_LRS eastus2; its access tier is checked by `apply`.

## ms-r7-m3-price-tts-2026-11-05 (2026-11-05, Retail Prices API, n = 2 reads)

Filter: `armRegionName eq 'centralindia' and contains(meterName,'Text To Speech')`.
- ServiceName 'Foundry Tools', product 'Azure Speech'.
- 'S1 Neural Text To Speech Characters': $15 per 1M (0f98e708-a16c-407b-8089-a0ed9e14ab49), the same in eastus2.
- Neural HD: $22 per 1M.

The keeper uses standard neural voices (hi-IN-SwaraNeural, en-IN-NeerjaNeural). It counts only the text's characters, a lower bound on what is billed.

## ms-r7-m3-price-models-2026-11-05 (2026-11-05, Retail Prices API, n = 2 reads)

Filter: `armRegionName eq 'eastus2' and contains(meterName,'5.6')`.
- gpt-5.6-luna ShortCo Std Gl (taxila-fast, DEPLOY_FAST): input $0.20, cached $0.02, output $1.20 per 1M (1e606a78 / 97d64f6e / 0edf673f).
- gpt-5.6-sol (taxila-brain, DEPLOY_BRAIN): $4 / $0.40 / $20.

These equal server/cost/prices.js, and the test asserts that. ServiceName is 'Foundry Models'. New 'Cd Wr' (cache write) meters exist; the keeper's prompts stay under the caching size.

## ms-r7-m3-jobs-fake-azure-2026-11-05 (2026-11-05, node --test, n = 15 tests)

tests/m3-plan.test.mjs runs both in-job scripts' main() against a fake Azure, with no network.

Keeper:
- The am run reached each target ($1.35 / $1.35 / $1.25) under the $2 cap. The ledger agreed with the fake's own spend to within 1e-3.
- The pm run made 0 new calls.
- With an unreadable ledger, a rerun did not spend again (one blind spend per day), and the pm run skipped with exit 1.
- Once the ledger read again, nothing was bought twice.
- A primary deployment that returned 400 three batches in a row fell back to taxila-brain.
- A ledger write lost after a batch left exit 1. The retry stayed under the cap.

Verifier:
- Read two Cost Management pages and printed M3-OK with streak 13 (start 2026-11-06, completes 2027-01-04).
- One service dipping still held the clock (5 left) but alerted services-below-min and portfolio-under-floor. Two dipping alerted streak-reset; a missing ledger alerted ledger-missing; a 403 alerted cost-query-failed.

The copies inside the self-contained jobs equal plan.js (toString for the verbatim ones, fixtures for the rest).

Not measured: anything live. The session had no Azure credentials.
md.open:
## open-r7-m3-verification-deadline (2026-11-05)

The Learn page (2026-11-03) says not qualifying for Milestone 3 within 180 days of business verification cancels the sponsorship. The sponsorship started 2026-07-08. If that was the verification day, the deadline is 2027-01-04, and the 60-day clock must start by 2026-11-06. The keeper cannot make day 1 earlier than the first full day after `apply`. Unknown: the real verification date, and whether the clause applies to sponsorships granted before it was published. The owner reads it in the Founders Hub portal (docs/design/round7/M3.md §1).
